daily.title: Gaza: Rains add misery to humanitarian catastrophe
daily.summary: With most homes damaged or destroyed by the war, Gazans are facing worsening humanitarian conditions due to heavy rain.

daily.title: 'Never Again!': Holocaust remembrance under pressure
daily.summary: Only a few Holocaust survivors remain who can share their stories firsthand. Meanwhile, voices calling for an end to what they describe as a "cult of guilt" are growing louder. How can Holocaust remembrance survive?

daily.title: Poland begins two days of mourning over Krakow shooting
daily.summary: Polish authorities have opened a terror probe after the shooting on Krakow's Main Square. Police confirmed that the bodies found at the suspect's home were those of his parents and sister.

daily.title: Germany news: Friedrich Merz set to confirm presidential nominee
daily.summary: The executive committee of the German chancellor's CDU party is expected to finalize its nomination for the country's president. DW has more.

daily.title: India: Delhi chokes on most polluted Diwali eve in 10 years
daily.summary: Delhi was ranked as the world's most polluted major city on the eve of Diwali. Delhi's air pollution is expected to get worse in the coming days. DW has more.

daily.title: As COP31 Antalya kicks off, can world move beyond big promises?
daily.summary: Droughts, floods and extreme heat are upping the pressure on delegates at the UN climate talks in Antalya, Turkey. Can countries move beyond pledges to concrete action?

daily.title: Poland: Gunman kills 6 in Krakow main square, police say
daily.summary: A suspect who fired from a car killed at least six people, including a British tourist, in Krakow's main market square. Officials said the man was fascinated with "radical" and "far-right" ideologies.

daily.title: Ebola: Why is there still no vaccine?
daily.summary: Ebola has been known about for decades, but there is still no vaccine against the Bundibugyo strain of the virus causing the current outbreak. New research raises hopes of protection against the various types of Ebola.

daily.title: Israeli president tasks Gadi Eisenkot with forming government
daily.summary: President Isaac Herzog has picked former Israeli military chief Gadi Eisenkot, leader of an anti-Netanyahu alliance, to take the first shot at trying to form a government. Tricky coalition talks are expected.

daily.title: Trump offers White House press secretary role to Dana White
daily.summary: US President Donald Trump has offered the White House press secretary job to Dana White, the chief executive of the Ultimate Fighting Championship. White has neither formally accepted nor turned down the invitation.

daily.title: France sees new round of Yellow Vest, student protests
daily.summary: Although fewer protesters turned out in comparison with previous weeks, several cities saw clashes between police and demonstrators.

daily.title: Armenia's selective prosecution: A threat to EU relations?
daily.summary: While Brussels has refrained from harsh criticism, Armenian civil society has warned of selective justice against opposition figures. Could the EU's pragmatic stance risk repeating past mistakes?

daily.title: South Africa's ANC facing worst-ever performance in local elections
daily.summary: Near-final results show South Africa's once dominant ANC will see its lowest-ever vote percentage. The party is taking the blame for shoddy municipal services, including water and electricity shortages.

daily.title: More than 40,000 gather as Pope Leo XIV celebrates Mass in Uruguay
daily.summary: Leo celebrated the first Mass of his South America tour less than a month after undergoing cancer surgery. He is seeking to raise interest in the Catholic Church in Uruguay, South America's most secular country.

daily.title: Journalism and AI: Who owns the news?
daily.summary: Publishers say AI chatbots are using their reporting to answer readers' questions while sending back less traffic and less money. Should the companies that build these tools pay for the journalism they rely on?

daily.title: Son of Iran's shah receives 'Freedom Prize' in Frankfurt
daily.summary: 18,000 people gathered in Frankfurt to show support for Reza Pahlavi, the son of the Iranian monarch ousted in 1979. Factions in the opposition have accused him of not distancing himself from his father's rule.

daily.title: After victory in the midterms, what next for US Democrats?
daily.summary: Donald Trump's Republican party has lost its majority in both chambers of the US Congress. But the president still has a lot of power — and the Democrats have yet to agree on how best to use theirs.

daily.title: Italy's Meloni blames pro-Russian hackers for cyberattack on minister
daily.summary: Antonio Tajani has said hackers published personal data stolen from him as Giorgia Meloni blamed pro-Russia criminals for the incident. The news follows a string of bomb threats that have grounded flights across the EU.

daily.title: Yemen: 33 killed in strike near Sanaa, Houthis say
daily.summary: The Iran-backed Houthi rebel group accused Saudi Arabia of hitting several homes in the village of al-Shariya near the Yemeni capital.

weekly.title: New Zealand election too close to call with over 95% of votes counted
weekly.summary: Initial results in New Zealand show the two main parties neck-and-neck with fewer than 4,000 votes separating them. Official results aren't expected until later this month once special votes have been counted.

weekly.title: Germany hopes to host world ice hockey championship — without Russia
weekly.summary: International protests continue after a court ruled that Russia must be allowed to return to international ice hockey. Germany is seeking a solution that will allow the country to host next year's world championship.

weekly.title: Ukraine: Russia hits Kyiv with airstrikes ahead of trilateral talks
weekly.summary: The strikes hit a major bridge and energy facilities in the Kyiv region. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy accused Moscow of trying to "push" Ukraine "into a blackout" ahead of talks in Abu Dhabi.

weekly.title: Amid protests, France's rising debt costs threaten stability
weekly.summary: France plans to spend an extra €4 billion on education amid nationwide protests. But with public debt mounting and interest costs climbing, how much fiscal room does the government have?

weekly.title: Ilse Aigner tipped by party allies as next German president
weekly.summary: German media reports suggest that Bavarian politician Ilse Aigner's chances of becoming the next president are on the up. Long favored by her Bavarian CSU, now it seems Christian Democrats nationwide plan to back her.

weekly.title: Tesla to 'wind down' production of flop Cybertruck
weekly.summary: Elon Musk's electric pickup for the future will start to be consigned to the past next year. The Cybertruck's bulk and crude shape meant it could only pass regulatory standards in more permissive markets.

weekly.title: Czech arms makers set sights on space defense in bid to sustain Ukraine-driven arms boom
weekly.summary: Czech arms makers have thrived on demand linked to the war in Ukraine. To sustain their growth, they need to look beyond ammunition and toward new technologies — and even space.

weekly.title: What to know about the IIHF Women's Ice Hockey World Championship
weekly.summary: As ice hockey's governing body continues to wrangle over how to respond to a CAS order to reinstate Russia to international play, the top women's tournament gets underway in Denmark without Russia.

weekly.title: Exercise coaching boosts colon cancer survival
weekly.summary: Evidence suggests exercise can keep more cancer patients alive. But what does "living longer" actually mean, and who does it apply to?

weekly.title: European shares join a global sell-off as AI spending fears rattle Wall Street and Asian markets
weekly.summary: European shares have fallen after sharp losses in Asia and on Wall Street. Doubts over huge AI investments and fears of curbs following the Democrats' US midterm victory have rattled global markets.

weekly.title: Arrests and investigations as Serbia begins postelection cleanup
weekly.summary: The landslide victory of the Student List in Serbia's general election seems to have removed a blockage in the justice system: Cases that were long stalled are now suddenly moving forward.

weekly.title: Germany’s Gen Z protests spark debate on integration, bias
weekly.summary: Political debate about the recent Gen Z riots have raised the question: Can Germany talk about problems with integration without putting entire groups of people under suspicion?

weekly.title: Russia is back in world sport, but who is drug testing its athletes?
weekly.summary: DW has found that three-quarters of Russia's weightlifting team had no independent out-of-competition testing before this year's world championships, despite the country's doping history.

weekly.title: Pioneering Jewish academy opens in Germany
weekly.summary: A Jewish academy has opened its doors in Frankfurt. The Central Council of Jews in Germany, the country’s leading Jewish umbrella group, set up the project to combat hate and promote dialogue and learning nationally.

weekly.title: Cristiano Ronaldo announces retirement from international football
weekly.summary: The announcement by the footballing legend comes just weeks after a public spat with Portugal coach Jorge Jesus over playing time.

weekly.title: Bomb threats disrupt several flights across Europe
weekly.summary: At least a dozen flights were either diverted or landed with a military escort after bomb or security threats. The first reported case involved a flight from Dublin to Rome landing outside Paris and more soon followed.

weekly.title: What the Democrats' midterms win means for the US economy and Trump
weekly.summary: From high oil prices and data centers to tariffs and mounting debt, economic concerns played a key role in the crushing defeat of President Donald Trump's Republicans. So can the Democrats now make a difference?

weekly.title: 36 years later: Hungary opens Communist-era secret service files
weekly.summary: Decades after the end of Soviet rule, Hungary is releasing all its secret service files. The disclosure is sparking fresh debate about informants, guilt and responsibility.

weekly.title: The 2011 discovery of neo-Nazi killers aired biases in German policing
weekly.summary: Many questions still surround the National Socialist Underground whose existence was revealed by neo-Nazi terrorist Beate Zschäpe on November 4, 2011. How has German society reacted to NSU crimes? Has justice been done?

weekly.title: Kosovo: Outrage as authorities accused of not helping femicide victim
weekly.summary: Despite reporting her husband to the police and pleading for protection, Arlinda Zekaj was brutally murdered. Now, thousands in Kosovo are protesting what they say is a dramatic failure of state institutions.

weekly.title: Gold for the West Bank: Meet Palestinian karate champ Mariam Bsharat
weekly.summary: The occupied West Bank is not an obvious breeding ground for sporting success. But Mariam Bsharat, 17, has beaten the odds to become a karate world champion and is making a new life in Germany.

weekly.title: Harry Potter films turns 25 ahead of new TV series' release
weekly.summary: In 2001, "Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone" hit cinemas and took the world by storm. Today, anticipation for the new series is high, but its creator, J.K. Rowling, remains a controversial figure.

weekly.title: Leading ice hockey nations, sponsors oppose Russia's return
weekly.summary: Ice hockey's governing body says the impact of a court decision forcing it to reinstate Russia presents "significant practical and sporting challenges." Several leading nations say they won't play against Russian teams.

weekly.title: BMW reports lower Q3 earnings as China woes mount
weekly.summary: BMW reports a drop in profits in the July to September quarter amid fierce competition from China.

weekly.title: Germany's celebrated children's author Janosch has died
weekly.summary: Bear, Tiger and Tiger-Duck: The author and illustrator Janosch achieved world fame with his heartwarming children's figures. He died at the age of 95.

weekly.title: From rotten food to political opponents: Researchers explore how disgust relates to our beliefs, and why the connection is complicated
weekly.summary: Some studies have linked disgust sensitivity to socially conservative attitudes. But does disgust shape our politics, or do our beliefs shape what we find disgusting?

weekly.title: How Berlin's Arab queers are building their community
weekly.summary: As the co-founder of the ADIRA Drag Festival, Lebanese performance artist, drag performer, DJ and cultural organizer Hassandra has become an essential part of Berlin's queer artistic landscape.

weekly.title: Cyprus: From ties with Russia to a strategic alignment with the US
weekly.summary: The Republic of Cyprus long balanced ties between Russia and the West. Now, it is phasing out Russian weapons, expanding defense cooperation with the United States and redefining its place in the Eastern Mediterranean.

weekly.title: Multiple flights to European airports targeted by bomb threats
weekly.summary: The bomb threats involved two passenger planes bound for Warsaw, a Ryanair flight from London to Spain, two flights to Rome and a flight traveling from Israel to the Bulgarian capital, Sofia. No explosives were found.

weekly.title: Football: Spanish player dies on after cardiac arrest on the pitch
weekly.summary: Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel has died following a collision with the opposing goalkeeper. The Spanish second-division club has said it is "heartbroken" by the loss.

weekly.title: Asian Cup postponed due to Middle East conflict
weekly.summary: The Asian Cup has become the latest sporting event to be affected by the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. Organizers cite "exceptional circumstances" in Saudi Arabia, which has seen several Houthi attacks of late.

weekly.title: Could the AI boom make borrowing more expensive in Europe?
weekly.summary: France, Germany and Italy face a volatile bond market as war inflation bites. With US tech giants now issuing billions in AI bonds, they are competing with cash-strapped European governments.

weekly.title: Germany news: Ukraine in focus at Berlin Security Conference
weekly.summary: A security conference in the German capital is addressing defending Europe against threats from Russia. Meanwhile, Germany's justice minister wants to raise penalties for sexual offenses. DW has more.

weekly.title: Ice hockey officials considering options after CAS order to reinstate Russia
weekly.summary: Ice hockey's ruling body is deciding how to respond to a decision by the Court of Arbitration for Sport that allows Russia back into international competition. Germany hasn't ruled out pulling out as a tournament host.

weekly.title: LA communities kick out Big Oil
weekly.summary: After years of advocacy from residents and legal battles with Big Oil, Los Angeles voted to ban drilling and phase out oil extraction in the city. It's the first city in the United States to kick the oil industry out.

weekly.title: Global pedestrian Karl Bushby returns home to UK after 28-year trek
weekly.summary: Karl Bushby, a British man who traveled 50,000 km without transport over the past 28 years, has come home. Starting in Chile, he crossed the Americas, Russia and parts of Central Asia and Europe — almost all on foot.

weekly.title: How Iliana Yotova won the presidential election in Bulgaria
weekly.summary: Iliana Yotova won the presidential election in Bulgaria, promising to be a "president of peace." But the campaign showed how divided Bulgarians are about the war in Ukraine and drone attacks in the Black Sea.

weekly.title: Merz says next German president 'must be a woman' — report
weekly.summary: German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier's second term is due to end in March next year. Meanwhile, Merz has called for 'digital sovereignty' in the era of AI.

weekly.title: Kimi Antonelli makes history as youngest F1 champion
weekly.summary: Kimi Antonelli became Formula One's youngest world champion and Italy's first since 1953 when he finished third in Sunday's thrilling and crash-hit Mexico City Grand Prix.

weekly.title: Russia's giant new radar in Kaliningrad raises alarm in NATO
weekly.summary: Russia is nearing completion of what experts think is a giant radar complex in Kaliningrad, capable of monitoring much of Europe. Experts warn the project could intensify the military standoff between Moscow and NATO.
